records.summary: The Prime Minister's Office records that the Prime Minister required the Supervisory Board (bankarad) of the Central Bank of Iceland to produce a written report on the Samherji hf. case following the Supreme Court judgment of 8 November 2018 in case no. 463/2017; the board's report reached the ministry on 21 February, and by letter dated 15 March the Prime Minister demanded further information, explanations and documents on three points: the administrative improvements at the bank announced in the board's report, the Director of Public Prosecutions' 2014 position on the validity of the penal provisions discussed at length in the Ombudsman of Althingi's opinion of 22 January 2019, and an alleged disclosure by Central Bank staff to RUV about a planned search of Samherji hf. on 27 March 2012 (the Ombudsman's letter of 4 March 2019). The bank's answers reached the ministry on 12 April and the ministry said it would make a final assessment in the following weeks of whether further data-gathering or responses were warranted. The page writes the first request as '12. november sl.' without a year; the year 2018 follows from the page's own date, 26 April 2019, and from the 8 November 2018 judgment the request followed, and is not printed on the page.
records.quote: Þann 12. nóvember sl. óskaði forsætisráðherra eftir greinargerð bankaráðs Seðlabanka Íslands um mál Samherja hf.
records.source_title: Svar Seðlabanka Íslands við erindi forsætisráðherra (Forsætisráðuneytið, 26 April 2019)

records.kind: statutory arrangement removing the bank's control of monetary policy
records.summary: The National Assembly's own notice of session 289, dated Tuesday 2 September 2014, records that the plenary resolved the executive's partial objection to the Codigo Monetario y Financiero and sent the text to the Registro Oficial for publication; legislators accepted 53 of the 56 observations by 94 votes in favour, 27 against and 2 abstentions, and ratified articles 18, 261 (except numeral 13) and 458 by 95 votes. The notice describes the code's Junta de Politica y Regulacion Monetaria y Financiera as a public-law legal person forming part of the Funcion Ejecutiva with administrative and financial autonomy, responsible for formulating policy and for regulating and supervising monetary, credit, exchange, financial, insurance and securities matters, with voting membership made up of the ministers responsible for economic policy, production, public finances and state planning plus a delegate of the President, while the Banco Central del Ecuador's general manager takes part in its deliberations with voice but no vote. This is filed as the 2014 legislative episode the Assembly's page describes; whether this allocation survives later Ecuadorean legislation was not tested and no claim is made that it is current law.
records.source_title: Asamblea Nacional resolvió objeción parcial al Código Monetario (Asamblea Nacional del Ecuador)

records.summary: Parliament of Uganda's own news service reports that on Tuesday 28 April 2026 Bank of Uganda Governor Michael Atingi-Ego, with Deputy Governor Prof. Augustus Nuwagaba and Executive Director for National Payment Systems Dr Twinemanzi Tumubweine, appeared before the joint Committee on Legal and Parliamentary Affairs and Committee on Defence and Internal Affairs on the Protection of Sovereignty Bill and told the committees that the bill could weaken the shilling, drain foreign reserves and undermine the central bank's constitutional independence. The assertions are the bank's, as reported by Parliament, not findings of Parliament: the Governor said the bill may conflict with article 162 of the Constitution, which protects the bank from direction or control by any person or authority, and that its parallel oversight and ministerial gatekeeping could interfere with the bank's exclusive mandate over monetary policy, exchange controls, banking supervision and financial stability. He also told MPs the bill's clause 13, criminalising publication of information that weakens the economic system, would damage market confidence, and that remittances of US$1.5 billion last year could fall if recipients of larger sums had to register. This is a draft law the bank objected to on the record before a parliamentary committee, not a law the bank asked for.
records.source_title: Central Bank weighs in on Sovereignty Bill, as Ugandan diaspora seek clarity (Parliament of Uganda, 28 April 2026)

records.summary: Forbes África Lusófona reports that the government of São Tomé and Príncipe dismissed Américo Barros as governor of the Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe, and that Prime Minister Jorge Bom Jesus said the dismissal followed Barros's political exposure during the MLSTP-PSD congress, which the government treated as conflicting with the central bank's organic law; the outlet quotes Bom Jesus saying the government had no alternative but to prepare the decree removing him, and reports Eugénio Soares, previously a member of the bank's board, as his replacement. A cause is therefore stated by the government and this is not an unexplained exit. The date 25 March 2022, a Friday, and the Council of Ministers session that approved the dismissal come from the same outlet's earlier report of 26 March 2022 ('Exonerado governador do Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe', https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=33544), which gives the government's first stated ground as a restructuring of the public sector; neither article names a decree number. Both sources are press reporting rather than a gazette or a decree, and no primary instrument was located.
records.source_title: Governo são-tomense diz que exposição política motivou exoneração do governador do banco central (Forbes África Lusófona, 1 April 2022)

blanks.read: CHL: two veins tested for a second episode beside the map's 2022 oficio to the Constitutional Convention. (1) Constitutional accusation (acusación constitucional) against Banco Central councillors: two searches surfaced only debate about whether the mechanism should exist, and the one piece read in full — Jaime Gajardo Falcón, opinion column, El Desconcierto, byline '6 de julio de 2021 - 23:00' (https://eldesconcierto.cl/2021/07/07/acusacion-constitucional-y-consejeros-del-banco-central) — is an opinion response to a José de Gregorio column of Monday 28 June arguing that the new Constitution should NOT allow accusations against councillors. No accusation was announced or filed; nothing to file. (2) ex-ante.cl's article on the ENADE debate over 'acusación contra consejeros del banco central' (https://www.ex-ante.cl/politica/enade-atria-y-hube-proyectan-duro-debate-por-acusacion-contra-consejeros-del-banco-central-y-el-mensaje-de-boeninguer-en-1999/) returned a client error through WebFetch and was not read. Chile is a publishing country and the pension-withdrawal reforms of 2020-2021 (Ley 21.253 and the retiro bills, on which the bank filed informes with Congress) were not opened this round; that is the next vein, and the question for it is whether a law OBLIGED the bank to do something it objected to in writing, or merely passed over its warning.

ETH: the parliamentary vein was tested and the document read states no move against the bank. Ethiopian News Agency, 'House Urges Central Bank to Maintain Tight Monetary Policy' (https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_6843068, dateline 27 June 2026) read in full: the House of People's Representatives' Plan, Budget and Finance Affairs Standing Committee, chaired by Dessalegn Wedajo, urged the National Bank of Ethiopia to STRENGTHEN the tight monetary policy it was already running, to expand lending to small enterprises and agriculture, and to look at measures helping domestic banks compete with newly admitted foreign banks. The committee's remarks are reported as largely positive about the bank's reforms and the article carries no criticism, no inquiry and no demand the bank opposed — a committee asking a bank to continue its own policy is not this row. The map's existing ETH record is the 2023 'MPs squeeze regulators' episode (thereporterethiopia.com/37670), which this is not.

LBR: a real second removal episode exists and is already on the map under the other row, so it is a duplicate. The July 2024 suspension of Central Bank of Liberia Executive Governor J. Aloysius Tarlue over a General Auditing Commission audit ('Liberia suspends central bank governor over audit', polity.org.za, 31 July 2024) is the exact source_url of have_cases.json LBR index 57 (Tarlue, 'election or budget financing', official finding, 2018-2024). The surrounding 2024-2025 items surfaced by search — the US$374k settlement package (allafrica 202502030288), President Boakai's January 2025 nomination of Henry Saamoi 'amid unresolved questions about Tarlue's status' (geezliberia), 'Induced Resignation?' (inprofiledailynews) — are later stages of that same affair rather than a distinct episode with its own actors and conduct, so none was filed. None of these pages was opened; the judgement is from the search titles plus the matching source URL.

AZE: searched for a state move on the bank beside the map's 2022 dismissal of the long-serving head — one search combining Aliyev, public criticism of the central bank, the 2015-2016 manat devaluations and the Chamber of Accounts. The results are all of the opposite shape: OCCRP/meydan.tv 'Azerbaijani insiders benefited from currency collapse' (June 2016), turan.az items in which an economist (Samir Aliyev) and an MP (Vahid Ahmedov) criticise the bank, RFE/RL on the bank denying devaluation rumours, and jam-news on a former opposition leader criticising reserves. Private and journalistic criticism of the bank is not an organ of the state acting on it, and the insider-profit story is the corruption row's shape, not this one. No state organ document was found; the Chamber of Accounts (Hesablama Palatası) own publications index was not opened and is the next vein.

COD: one search of the Inspection Générale des Finances / Assemblée nationale route beside the map's 2026 Cour des comptes audit mission. The live item it surfaced is 'Congo-Kinshasa: Le gouverneur Grâce Nkuanga Bilolo entendu par la justice dans une affaire de présumé détournement' (fr.allafrica.com/stories/202602100143.html, not opened) with mediacongo and afrik.com companions on the justice system investigating opaque practices at the Banque Centrale and Gécamines. That is a prosecution of individuals for their own conduct, which this row expressly refuses, and it belongs on the corruption-case row where the DRC already holds three Mutombo records; Nkuanga Bilolo appears on neither row and is a live corruption-row lead for a later round. No IGF or parliamentary commission report naming the BCC as its subject was located.

GIN: one search for a dismissal by decree after the map's December 2021 junta clear-out. It returned the 2021 episode itself (financialafrik 8 December 2021; africanews 'Guinea junta dismisses head of the central bank'; centralbanking.com 7906496) plus one possible second episode, afrique-sur7 'Guinée : Mamadi Doumbouya limoge le directeur de la Banque centrale' (https://www.afrique-sur7.fr/483357-guinee-mamadi-doumbouya-banque-centrale), which failed with a client error through WebFetch and was not read, so neither its date nor whom it concerns is known. Two BCRG-hosted PDFs also surfaced and were not opened ('Hommage au Gouverneur Nfaly SANGARE', December 2025, and a March 2026 note on honours for BCRG managers), which between them may date a change of governor. Guinea is untested rather than empty.

SMR: one search in Italian for the government removing or directing the Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino, beside the map's 2005 statute record. Every result was a bare consigliograndeegenerale.sm document id (documento17076429, 17076408, 17002494, 17026406 and others) with no title text in the search output, so nothing could be chosen to fetch and no document was opened. The route for a later round is the Consiglio Grande e Generale's own 'lavori consiliari / consultazione archivi' index rather than a keyword search, which returns opaque ids on this host.

TLS: one search of the Parlamento Nacional route beside the map's 2005 statute record. Two unopened candidates: Tatoli, 'National Parliament approves general framework for the financial system and banking activities', 14 July 2026 (https://en.tatoli.tl/2026/07/14/national-parliament-approves-general-framework-for-the-financial-system-and-banking-activities/17/), and the Jornal da República issues it would appear in (mj.gov.tl/jornal/public/docs/2026/serie_1/SERIE_I_NO_32.pdf). Neither was fetched, so whether the new framework law moves any power away from the BCTL, and whether the BCTL objected, is untested. Budget went to the four countries that converted.

HKG: no fetch spent, because the obvious second episode is already on the map under the other row. The Legislative Council's Lehman Brothers minibond inquiry, which is the one state-organ proceeding against the HKMA that Hong Kong's record offers, is have_cases.json HKG index 175 (Joseph Yam Chi-kwong, 'rescues or hidden losses', official finding, 2012, source scmp.com/article/1003321/lehman-criticism-played-down) — the same episode under a different description, so filing the LegCo select-committee report as a removals-row event would duplicate it. searched.json also records (r71) that the Audit Commission vein is closed by the inversion test: the HKMA is not among the 86 accounts its Director of Audit certifies. A genuinely distinct Hong Kong episode would have to come from LegCo motions or the Financial Secretary's directions to the Exchange Fund, neither of which was opened.

Not reached at all, no document opened, budget exhausted: AIA ATG KNA VCT (all four hold only the one expanded ECCB 'public pressure' record of 17 February 2025, so a national finding would be each one's first own record and the route is each island's parliament/Hansard, not the ECCB), BFA, BLZ, BRN, COM, CUB, DJI, GNQ, JOR, LVA, MDG, MRT, NAM, OMN, QAT, SGP, SWZ, ZMB. Two of these were costed and deliberately dropped rather than forgotten: LVA, where the live candidate is the Court of Justice judgment of 26 February 2019 in C-202/18 Rimšēvičs v Latvia annulling KNAB's decision barring the governor from performing his duties — a state organ removing a governor from office, but arguably the same Rimšēvičs episode as have_cases.json LVA index 60, so it needs a curator's ruling before a fetch is spent; and MDG, where have_cases.json already holds the 2026 allegation of political pressure on Governor Andrianarivelo to release central bank funds, so the obvious removals-row candidate there is that same episode.

checked_not_in_assignment: None. No country outside the 34-code assignment was researched, searched or filed this round.
leads_not_opened: ISL: the two documents the Prime Minister's Office page links but which 404 to curl and to WebFetch — 'Bréf forsætisráðherra til Seðlabanka Íslands' (the 15 March 2019 letter itself, https://www.stjornarradid.is/library/01--Frettatengt---myndir-og-skrar/FOR/Br%c3%a9f%20fors%c3%a6tisr%c3%a1%c3%b0herra%20til%20S%c3%8d%20dags.%2015.%20mars%202019.pdf, HTTP 404, 0 bytes to curl) and 'Greinargerð bankaráðs Seðlabanka Íslands'. Anyone re-checking will need the ministry's current file paths.

ISL: the Ombudsman of Althingi (umboðsmaður Alþingis) opinion of 22 January 2019 and letter of 4 March 2019 on the Central Bank's foreign-exchange enforcement, both named on the ministry page but not opened. If the opinion makes a finding against the bank in its own voice, that is a second Icelandic record on this row and a separate oversight-organ episode from the Prime Minister's examination filed above.

ISL: Þingskjal 845 of the 149th Althingi session (https://www.althingi.is/altext/149/s/0845.html) was opened and is the Prime Minister's ANSWER to Birgir Þórarinsson's written question on the Central Bank's gjaldeyriseftirlit — case counts, fines paid to the treasury, cases overturned by the courts, complaints, claims against the bank and the cost of the function. The replies were supplied by the bank itself. A written question answered is parliamentary scrutiny, not a state organ acting against the bank, so nothing was filed; but the answer's own figures on cases overturned by the courts and on monetary claims against the bank are a live lead for a different row.

UGA: the later stages of the Protection of Sovereignty Bill were not opened — Cabinet's 4 May 2026 meeting to finalise it (allafrica 202605040025) and 'Uganda passes softened sovereignty bill' (theafricanmirror). Whether the enacted law kept clause 13 or the provisions the bank objected to is untested, and the enactment would be a separate dated step from the 28 April objection filed above.

ECU: current force not verified. The record filed is the National Assembly's own account of the 2 September 2014 enactment. Ecuador's 2021 'Ley para la defensa de la dolarización' (primicias.ec items surfaced in the same search) reorganised the Junta and the BCE's governance and was not read; a later round should establish whether the 2014 allocation still stands before any standing-arrangement claim is made.

STP: no primary instrument. Neither Forbes África Lusófona article names a decree number for Américo Barros's exoneração, and the Diário da República of São Tomé and Príncipe was not searched. The bank's organic law, which the Prime Minister is reported to have invoked against the governor's party candidacy, was also not read.
